items.followUp: Write two uses of enzymes in daily life or industry.

rubric.why: Award for one correct general function or use of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes speed up biochemical reactions by lowering their activation energy.
rubric.how: Give one mark for stating that enzymes catalyse or speed up reactions, or lower activation energy.

rubric.why: Award for a distinct practical use of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes are used in applications such as digestion, food processing, detergents or medicine.
rubric.how: Give one mark for naming one correct application.

modelAnswer: Enzymes act as biological catalysts and speed up biochemical reactions in living organisms.
Enzymes are used in industry, for example in detergents to help remove stains.

items.followUp: State two properties of water that help produce transpiration pull.

rubric.why: Cohesion keeps water molecules connected in a continuous column.
rubric.description: Cohesion between water molecules helps maintain a continuous column of water in xylem.
rubric.how: Give one mark for identifying cohesion or the attraction between water molecules.

rubric.why: Adhesion helps water remain attached to the xylem walls as it is pulled upward.
rubric.description: Adhesion between water molecules and xylem walls helps support the water column.
rubric.how: Give one mark for identifying adhesion or the attraction of water to xylem walls.

modelAnswer: Cohesion between water molecules keeps them joined as a continuous column in the xylem.
Adhesion between water molecules and the xylem walls helps the water column resist breaking as it is pulled upward.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell membrane and explain why it is called selectively permeable.

rubric.why: The membrane forms the cell's outer boundary and separates its contents from the surroundings.
rubric.description: The cell membrane encloses the cell and separates its contents from the external environment.
rubric.how: Give one mark for a correct boundary or separation function.

rubric.why: Regulating exchange is a key membrane function.
rubric.description: The membrane selectively controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
rubric.how: Give one mark for stating that it regulates what enters or leaves the cell.

rubric.why: The bilayer is the basic structural framework in the fluid mosaic model.
rubric.description: The membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.how: Give one mark for naming the phospholipid bilayer.

rubric.why: Proteins distributed in the bilayer give the membrane its mosaic appearance.
rubric.description: Different proteins are embedded in or associated with the phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.how: Give one mark for describing the membrane proteins.

rubric.why: The fluid mosaic model explains both the mobility of its components and its varied appearance.
rubric.description: Lipids and some proteins can move within the membrane, making it fluid; the scattered proteins create a mosaic pattern.
rubric.how: Give one mark for explaining fluidity and/or the mosaic arrangement.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane forms the boundary of the cell and separates its contents from the external environment.
It is selectively permeable and controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
In the fluid mosaic model, the membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer.
Different protein molecules are embedded in or associated with the bilayer, giving it a mosaic appearance.
The lipids and some proteins can move within the membrane, so it is fluid.

items.followUp: State four ways in which biodiversity benefits people or ecosystems.

rubric.why: Biodiversity supports balanced and stable ecosystems.
rubric.description: Biodiversity helps maintain ecosystem balance and stability.
rubric.how: Give one mark for a correct ecosystem benefit.

rubric.why: Living organisms provide resources used by people.
rubric.description: Biodiversity is a source of useful products such as food, medicines, fuel and timber.
rubric.how: Give one mark for naming a useful biological resource.

rubric.why: Biodiversity supports livelihoods and economic activity.
rubric.description: Biodiversity has economic value and can provide income, employment or tourism opportunities.
rubric.how: Give one mark for a correct economic benefit.

rubric.why: Biodiversity supplies genetic resources and essential ecosystem services.
rubric.description: Biodiversity provides genetic resources or services such as pollination and nutrient cycling.
rubric.how: Give one mark for a further distinct benefit or ecosystem service.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity helps maintain the balance and stability of ecosystems.
It provides useful resources such as food, medicines, fuel and timber.
It has economic value and supports livelihoods, employment and tourism.
It provides genetic resources and ecosystem services such as pollination and nutrient cycling.

items.followUp: Explain the role of chlorophyll and water in the light reactions of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: The light reactions begin when chlorophyll absorbs light energy.
rubric.description: Chlorophyll in photosystem II absorbs light energy.
rubric.how: Give one mark for identifying light absorption by chlorophyll, especially in photosystem II.

rubric.why: Water splitting replaces electrons and releases oxygen and hydrogen ions.
rubric.description: Water is split by photolysis, releasing electrons, hydrogen ions and oxygen.
rubric.how: Give one mark for photolysis or its products.

rubric.why: Electron transfer supports ATP formation.
rubric.description: Electrons pass along an electron transport chain, and their energy is used to form ATP.
rubric.how: Give one mark for electron transport or ATP production linked to it.

rubric.why: Light re-energises electrons in photosystem I, which help reduce NADP.
rubric.description: Electrons reach photosystem I, are re-energised by light and are used to form NADPH.
rubric.how: Give one mark for photosystem I or NADPH formation.

rubric.why: A clear, labelled sequence diagram should show the main inputs, pathway and products.
rubric.description: Diagram shows the light reactions in sequence, including water, light, electron transport, ATP, NADPH and oxygen.
rubric.how: Give one mark for a coherent labelled flow diagram with key products.

modelAnswer: Light is absorbed by chlorophyll in photosystem II (PSII), exciting electrons.
Water undergoes photolysis, releasing electrons, hydrogen ions and oxygen.
The electrons pass along an electron transport chain; their energy is used to make ATP.
Light excites electrons again in photosystem I (PSI); these electrons help reduce NADP to NADPH.
Diagram: Light → PSII → electron transport chain → PSI → NADP⁺ → NADPH; H₂O → PSII (electrons and H⁺) and O₂ is released; electron transport drives ADP + Pi → ATP.

items.followUp: Define organic compounds and state what elements are commonly found in them.

rubric.why: Bioelements are the elements that make up living organisms.
rubric.description: Bioelements are the chemical elements present in or required to make living organisms.
rubric.how: Give one mark for a definition identifying them as elements of living organisms.

rubric.why: Biomolecules are compounds found in organisms and formed from bioelements.
rubric.description: Biomolecules are chemical compounds of living organisms, formed from bioelements.
rubric.how: Give one mark for defining biomolecules as compounds of living organisms.

modelAnswer: Bioelements are the chemical elements that make up living organisms.
Biomolecules are the chemical compounds of living organisms, formed from bioelements.

items.followUp: Name one contribution of Abdul Malik Asmai and one book he wrote.

rubric.why: Asmai is noted for his contributions to the study of animals and zoology.
rubric.description: Abdul Malik Asmai was famous for his contributions to zoology and the study of animals.
rubric.how: Give one mark for identifying his work on animals or zoology.

rubric.why: A correct title of one of his books earns the second mark.
rubric.description: One of his books was Kitab al-Khail (Book of Horses), Kitab al-Ibil (Book of Camels), or Kitab al-Wuhush (Book of Wild Animals).
rubric.how: Give one mark for naming any one correct book.

modelAnswer: Abdul Malik Asmai is famous for his contributions to zoology and the study of animals.
One of his books is Kitab al-Khail (Book of Horses).

items.followUp: Define biotechnology and state one way it is used.

rubric.why: Pharmacology concerns drugs and their effects.
rubric.description: Pharmacology is the study of drugs and their effects on living organisms.
rubric.how: Give one mark for defining pharmacology in terms of drugs and their effects.

rubric.why: Biotechnology applies organisms, cells or biological processes to make useful products.
rubric.description: Biotechnology is the use of living organisms, cells or biological processes to produce useful products.
rubric.how: Give one mark for a definition that includes biological materials or processes used for a practical purpose.

modelAnswer: Pharmacology is the study of drugs and their effects on living organisms.
Biotechnology is the use of living organisms, cells or biological processes to produce useful products.
